task_description: The task asks for the scheduled Pompano Beach arrival time of whichever Tri-Rail train carried the most passengers on May 27, 2019, formatted as a 12-hour clock time with AM/PM (no leading zero). The gold answer, 6:41 PM, is the scheduled Pompano Beach arrival of that single highest-ridership train, a number that lives in a train-level ridership breakdown (a 'system usage by train' table) cross-referenced against the timetable for that date.
final_vs_expected: produced None (run hit the 900s timeout with zero FINAL ANSWER) vs gold 6:41 PM — the team never emitted any answer at all.
primary_cause: A single agent (WebResearcher) was the only one ever selected; it could not locate the May-2019 train-level ridership PDF and looped on near-identical searches for 18 rounds until the wall-clock cap, so the run timed out with no answer and no other role ever activated.
mast_rationale: 1.5 (unaware of termination/finalize path): only WebResearcher ever speaks; the selector never routes to Finalizer, and WebResearcher never publishes a candidate answer or hands off, so the run never moves toward FINAL ANSWER and dies on the cap. 1.3 (step repetition): rounds re-issue functionally identical queries ('May 27 2019 Tri-Rail ... Pompano Beach passengers', '05MAY2019.pdf', 'SYSTEM USAGE BY TRAIN') over and over across both turns, repeatedly hitting the same March-2019 PDF and Etsy junk. 3.1 (premature termination — degenerate): the run ends (by timeout) with the task unsolved; no verification stage ever reached. 2.3 (mild task derailment): late rounds drift into guessing peak-hour trains ('maybe P617', '7:50 AM train') instead of staying on the one needed datum. NOTE these are mostly single-agent/structural symptoms, not inter-agent ones.
trace_narrative: Turn 1: the selector routes to WebResearcher, which runs 9 internal rounds of web_search / fetch_url trying to find a May-27-2019 Tri-Rail train-level ridership figure. It only ever surfaces the March 2019 operations PDF (03MAR2019.pdf), generic schedule pages, Wikipedia, and SEO-spam Etsy listings. fetch_url on the ridership page returns boilerplate; the April PDF returns raw binary; an archive.org schedule PDF times out. Its sole published message in Turn 1 is not prose to teammates but a raw tool-call JSON blob (three more web_search queries) — i.e. it published its internal tool intent, not a finding. Turn 2: the selector's own reasoning ('we don't have actual results yet, continuing web research seems the right path') re-selects WebResearcher, which runs another 9 rounds of the same searches, fails to fetch 05MAY2019.pdf (404), and drifts into speculating about peak-hour trains (P601/P617). It finally publishes an honest 'I couldn't verify which specific Tri-Rail train carried the most passengers ... so I can't give a reliable Pompano Beach arrival time without guessing,' listing schedule times and inviting the user to supply the report. No Analyst, Critic, or Finalizer is ever selected; the run hits 900s timeout with no FINAL ANSWER. agents that spoke = 1.
open_ended_diagnosis: This is a structural-nonconvergence + single-agent-capability failure, not inter-agent misalignment — there is essentially no inter-agent dynamic to misalign, because only one of four agents ever acted. The root datum (the May-2019 train-level ridership breakdown) was never retrievable through the search/fetch tools available: the canonical source 05MAY2019.pdf 404s, the April PDF returns unparsed binary (the harness has no PDF text extraction), and search only ever returns the March PDF, schedule pages, and Etsy spam. WebResearcher correctly recognized the limit ('there's no direct data available, so I need to be honest about that') and ultimately published an honest non-answer rather than fabricating — that is good single-agent behavior, not a distortion. The decisive failure is the selector loop: with no usable result, the selector kept re-picking WebResearcher ('continuing web research seems the right path') instead of routing to Analyst (which has run_python and could have attempted PDF parsing of the binary the WebResearcher had already fetched) or letting WebResearcher hand its partial findings to a finalizer to at least produce a best-effort answer. Two further harness-level pathologies amplify the loss: (1) WebResearcher's Turn-1 'published' message is a raw {"tool_uses":[...]} JSON blob — its internal tool-call plan leaked into the published channel rather than a human-readable finding, so even if a peer had been listening they'd receive query strings, not evidence; (2) the absence of PDF text extraction made the one promising lead (the operations PDFs) a dead end. None of this is information withholding, ignored input, ToM failure, or reasoning-action mismatch — the private reasoning and the eventual published message are consistent (both say 'I can't verify this'), and there was no second agent to be misaligned with.
reasoning_vs_published: Private vs published is consistent, so no 2.4/2.6. In Turn 2 round 1 WebResearcher privately reasons 'there's no direct data available, so I need to be honest about that. I'm guessing the train with the most passengers was P603' — and its final published message faithfully reports the same uncertainty: 'I couldn't verify which specific Tri-Rail train carried the most passengers on May 27, 2019 from the accessible sources I found, so I can't give a reliable Pompano Beach arrival time without guessing.' The private guesses (P603, P617, P601) were NOT smuggled into the published answer as if certain — the agent suppressed its speculation appropriately, the opposite of info-distortion. The one genuine communication defect is in Turn 1: the published channel contains a raw tool-call JSON blob (`{"tool_uses":[{"recipient_name":"functions.web_search",...}]}`) rather than any synthesized finding — but this reaches no peer (none is selected next except WebResearcher itself), so it causes no downstream misuse; it is a harness/serialization artifact, not a deliberate withholding. The selector's reasoning is explicit about why it never diversifies: 'we don't have actual results yet, continuing web research seems the right path' — i.e. the misrouting is the selector defaulting to the same role, not any agent distorting or ignoring another's input.
